findings.criterion: 3 (latch cannot be burned hermetically) and 4 (history recovered)
findings.section: Phase 2 (Phase 1 — CAS + hermetic beacon) / Phase 7 (Phase 6 — backfill)
findings.message: Phase 2 locks CAS consumption to a positive identity: "only a finalize presenting the matching beacon may consume the CAS; any non-beacon context records retryable NON-TERMINAL finalize-deferred." Phase 6's backfill tool, by its own run discipline, executes only while the service is UNREACHABLE — i.e., when no live beacon exists — yet claims to "use the IDENTICAL exclusive-create claim files as the live path" and to reuse "the Phase-1 claim path verbatim, no new code path." These cannot both be true. Either the backfill bypasses the beacon predicate (a second consumption path, which reintroduces exactly the "compare-and-decide code path" idea 14 boasts does not exist, and creates a template for any future hermetic context to burn the latch by imitating the backfill), or the backfill honestly hits the beacon gate and defers every record it tries to mint, making criterion 4 unachievable. The plan must define a distinct, explicitly-scoped backfill authority (e.g., beacon-absent + terminal-status + `measured-backfill`-only writes) and regression-test THAT predicate — right now the two phases quietly assume incompatible admission rules for the same primitive.

findings.section: Phase 4 (Phase 3 — forward swarm capture), Deferred items
findings.message: Criterion 1's first clause is unconditional: "Swarm launches pin --session-id." The North Star's "where wired" qualifier modifies FINALIZE ownership, not pinning. The draft's deferral — "orchestrators not yet routed through the helper … covered by the reconcile-dead catch-all + orphan sweep until refactored" — silently converts unconditional pinning into partial pinning, because an orchestrator not routed through the helper does not pin at all. The claimed safety nets do not hold for that population: the reconcile-dead finalize needs a correlatable session id to find a sidecar, and the orphan sweep keys on a worktree-dirname session marker that an unpinned, un-helper'd launch has no reason to produce. The intake evidence says 106 of 111 sessions are swarm — the exact population this criterion exists for — so "which are wired this effort vs later" is not an enumeration detail to punt to Stage 2; it is the difference between meeting and not meeting criterion 1. Worse, the deferral contradicts the phase's own conformance test ("greps product code for raw spawn calls outside the helper and fails on any hit"): if unrouted orchestrators survive the wave, that test is either red or scope-blind (e.g., skill-layer launches outside Anchor product code — which is likely where the 106 swarm sessions came from). The plan must state which launch surfaces the helper can actually reach, and show that the unreachable ones still pin.

findings.criterion: 3 (latch cannot be burned) and 4 (never overwrites a live-measured record)
findings.section: Phase 2 (repair path for the 3 poisoned records)
findings.message: The plan simultaneously asserts (a) "a finalized cost file is never rewritten — byte-identical content + stable mtime across a second finalize attempt" (mitigation 16), (b) "an existing live-measured cost file wins BY CONSTRUCTION — no compare-and-decide code path exists" (idea 14), and (c) a repair path that "reclassifies" the 3 `sidecar-root-unavailable` records to `finalize-deferred` so backfill "may still measure them." For those 3 sessions the latch was already CONSUMED (intake evidence) — meaning some artifact of consumption exists. If, under the new scheme, that consumption maps to an existing claim/cost file, then by (a) and (b) the backfill's exclusive-create will lose to the poisoned artifact and the sessions stay unmeasured — the repair is dead on arrival. If instead the repair deletes or supersedes the poisoned artifact, then a "rewrite a consumed latch" code path exists, and (a)/(b) are false as universal claims — and that path needs its own guard so only THIS class of record is ever repairable, or the never-overwrite guarantee for live-measured records rests on convention rather than construction. The draft never says which; the ambiguity sits precisely on the highest-risk primitive the risk taxonomy names.

The inversion from blocklist to positive identity only works if beacon ISSUANCE is itself positively scoped, and the draft never specifies that. The healthcheck boots a real throwaway server on 8778 running the same anchor_gui boot path; preview servers boot the same code on OS-assigned ports. If "the live NSSM service writes a boot beacon at startup" is implemented as "server boot writes a beacon," every hermetic server is a beacon-holder and the poison vector recurs wearing a badge. If issuance is instead gated on "not healthcheck, not redirected data dir, not test port," the design has smuggled the blocklist back in — the exact enumerate-the-hermetic-contexts fragility idea 5 claims to eliminate. The predicate needs a stated positive anchor (e.g., beacon written iff the process holds the exclusive 8777 bind on the real data dir, verified at write time), and the STUB-GATE trio needs a fourth case: a fully-booted NON-8777 server attempting finalize with its own self-issued beacon must defer. Without that case, the regression tests validate the mechanism against the previous failure's shape, not the next one's.

The phase promises to "verify count ≥ the 55 observed at intake" and to "log any dirs present-then vs present-now delta honestly in the manifest." This is unfalsifiable as written: the intake evidence recorded a COUNT ("55+ sidecar dirs"), not an enumeration of dirnames. Without a then-list, a per-dir delta cannot be computed, and "count ≥ 55" cannot detect a prune-and-grow substitution (e.g., 10 historical dirs pruned since 2026-07-18 while 12 new ones appeared — the check passes while history criterion 4 depends on is already gone). The honest version of this task is: snapshot NOW, enumerate what was captured, and state plainly that losses between intake and snapshot are UNDETECTABLE — reconciling instead against the registry's known session-id set (which sessions have a matching archived dir vs not) to bound what the backfill can possibly recover. As drafted, the manifest performs an audit it lacks the evidence to perform, which is exactly the kind of confidence-without-provenance this North Star exists to eliminate.

The backfill tool "REFUSES to run while the service is reachable unless --force," but the phase ordering puts the backfill run (Phase 6) BEFORE merge+deploy (Phase 7), while the production service is live on 8777 throughout the build. The plan therefore never says when the required service outage happens: either a build wave takes production down mid-effort (unstated, and it should be a deliberate, drained stop per the warm-restart convention), or the backfill actually runs inside Phase 7's deploy window (making the phase ordering wrong as written), or — the failure mode the discipline exists to prevent — the builder reaches for `--force` because the refusal fires on the first real run. A run-discipline feature whose happy path is unreachable in the plan's own sequence trains the operator to use the escape hatch. Name the outage: when, how (drain), and which phase owns it.

The sweep mints `measured-backfill` records for sidecars "whose dirname embeds a valid session marker but has no registry row," claiming "an unregistered launch degrades to late-measured, never invisible." But the Phase-2 frozen record schema requires `lane`, `effort_id`/`chain_id`, and the rollup surfaces are per-project per-lane — a session with no registry row has none of these. Where does this record actually SURFACE? If nowhere, "never invisible" is an assertion about a file on disk, not about spend a user can see, and the criterion is met in letter only. Specify the attribution fallback (e.g., an "unattributed" line on the rollup) or honestly rename the guarantee. Relatedly, the `id-unverified` path (idea 1) never states whether such a session's spend is measured under the observed id or excluded — same ambiguity, same fix needed.

File EXISTENCE under `.anchor/run-costs/` IS the CAS. The plan says a non-beacon context "records retryable NON-TERMINAL usage_state: finalize-deferred" — but never says WHERE. If the deferral stamp is written anywhere on the claim path, the act of deferring consumes the latch, recreating the original bug with a politer label. The plan must pin the invariant explicitly — deferred/skipped/unrecognized states live ONLY on the registry record; the claim file is created by nothing except a successful measured write — and the STUB-GATE hermetic-skip test must assert the claim file's NON-existence after the skip, not merely that a later finalize succeeds.

The predicate is defined as "an explicit synthetic=True registration flag … never name-sniffing," yet the convention test promises that "registering synthetic without the flag fails loudly." Detecting an UNflagged synthetic registration requires recognizing syntheticness by some signal other than the flag — i.e., name-sniffing, the thing just forbidden. As written the test is unimplementable; what's actually implementable is (a) the known synthetic REGISTRARS (doctor, healthcheck) are asserted to pass the flag, and (b) all surfaces route through the predicate. Say that instead. Separately, "__doctor__ migrates onto the flag" is stated as code behavior but the registry already CONTAINS historical `__doctor__` rows without the flag — the exclusion of criterion 2 needs a data migration (or a one-time legacy shim, honestly labeled), not just new registration code.

"Fixture-test a cache-read-dominated session and a mixed-model session; assert each estimate stays within a declared error band" — within a band relative to WHAT ground truth? There is no external reference for a subscription-equivalent estimate; the test necessarily computes the expected value from the same table and formula it is testing, proving arithmetic determinism, not estimate validity. A skeptical reader should not be shown "error band" language that implies calibration that doesn't exist. Either declare the honest test (golden-value regression pinning the formula against hand-computed fixtures, so a table or formula change turns a test red) or, if a real band is intended, name its reference point. The "est." label carries the honesty load here — don't let the test suite overclaim what the label correctly underclaims.

"Pin a CAPTURED REAL sidecar as a test fixture" commits a real engine transcript — conversation content, file paths, potentially secrets from whatever that historical session touched — into the repo. The project runs a no-PII/secrets scan in `distro.py` and this repo already leaks-by-default per the 2026-07-17 review; a raw sidecar fixture is a new instance of the same class. The fixture's VALUE is its field shape and envelope names, not its content — the plan should require a shape-preserving sanitization step (real structure, scrubbed strings, token counts kept) and state that the fixture passes the distro scan. Cheap to fix now, expensive after it's committed.

Every heading carries two conflicting ordinals ("Phase 1 — Phase 0 — …" through "Phase 8 — Phase 7 — …"), and the success-criteria block appears twice (verbatim North Star + a paraphrased summary). Stage 2 wave mapping, Foreman handoff, and Shark convergence all key on phase identity; an off-by-one label scheme invites cross-references to the wrong phase. Pick one numbering and delete the duplicate criteria block.

findings.criterion: 3 (latch cannot be burned hermetically) and 4 (history recovered)
findings.message: The plan contradicts itself on who may consume the CAS. Phase 2 locks consumption to "only a finalize presenting the matching beacon" — a boot beacon written by the live NSSM service — and routes every non-beacon context to `finalize-deferred`. Phase 7's backfill tool then, BY DESIGN, runs while the service is DOWN (it probes 8777 and refuses to run if reachable) and "uses the IDENTICAL exclusive-create claim files as the live path." A stopped service means no valid beacon (dead PID, stale token), so under the Phase-2 predicate as written the backfill is structurally a non-beacon context and cannot mint a single record — criterion 4 is unimplementable against criterion 3's own mechanism. The same hole swallows every other legitimate out-of-process writer: the warm-drain script (`pre_restart_drain.py`, a separate elevated process), any future CLI-side finalize, the forced backfill mode. The plan needs an explicit authorization story (e.g., beacon-OR-service-verifiably-down, or a distinct backfill credential) specified now, not discovered at Foreman time. A competitor plan would define the trust model for ALL writers, not just the happy-path service process.

Phase 0 copies "every sidecar dir whose dirname embeds an `…anchor-worktrees-<session_id>` munged cwd" — i.e., it FILTERS at snapshot time using a munging matcher that isn't isolated and regression-tested until Phase 2/3. This inverts the whole rationale for snapshotting NOW. If the preliminary matcher misses a dirname variant (different munging across engine versions, path-length truncation, casing), the excluded dirs are then pruned by engine retention and are gone forever — the exact irreversible loss the snapshot exists to prevent — and no later phase can detect the omission because the evidence no longer exists. The snapshot must be OVER-inclusive (copy the entire sidecar root, or at minimum everything matching a maximally loose pattern) and defer all filtering to Phase 6 where the hardened matcher lives. Bytes are cheap; a false-negative at snapshot time is permanent. The "verify count ≥ 55" check does not save this: it validates the matcher against itself.

The choke-point launch helper plus a "conformance test [that] greps PRODUCT CODE for raw spawn calls" structurally cannot cover the dominant swarm source: skill-layer dispatch (the 5:1 agy/orchestrator pattern), where sub-agent CLI processes are spawned by the model INSIDE a session, not by Anchor product code. That is precisely how the 106 observed swarm sessions came to exist unmeasured. The plan's own deferral ("orchestrators not yet routed through the helper… enumeration in Stage 2") quietly punts the enumeration that decides whether criterion 1 is met at all — and the Phase-8 live proof ("trigger one small real fleet run and confirm measured records") has no stated fallback if that run's launcher turns out to be unwired. A competitor plan would name the concrete launch surfaces (which orchestrators, which dispatcher scripts) in the MASTER plan and state which are in-scope, because "where wired" with an empty wired set trivially satisfies the letter of the criterion while producing zero new measured swarm records. Demand the enumeration be a Stage-1 commitment, not a Stage-2 discovery.

The synthetic predicate is "driven by an explicit `synthetic=True` registration flag (marker convention, NEVER name-sniffing)." But every `__doctor__` session already in the registry was registered before the flag existed and carries no marker — under a strict never-name-sniff rule those legacy records classify as non-synthetic and LEAK into every spend surface, directly violating "excluded everywhere." The plan needs a named one-shot migration stamping the flag onto existing doctor records (which unavoidably identifies them by name — acceptable as a one-time migration, but it must be admitted and specified, not left to collide with the stated rule). Relatedly, the loud-failure test ("registering synthetic without the flag fails loudly") is circular as written: detecting an unflagged synthetic registration requires exactly the name-sniffing the convention forbids. Specify what actually enforces it.

findings.criterion: 1 and 4 (every class of run session measured or honestly reported)
findings.message: Sessions that finish AFTER the Phase-0 snapshot but BEFORE the Phase-3 substrate deploys fall through every net in the plan: they are not in the frozen snapshot (backfill reads the snapshot "exclusively"), live finalize didn't exist when they ended, the orphan sweep explicitly targets only sidecars "with no registry row" (these sessions HAVE rows), and reconcile-dead finalize fires on the transition, which already happened pre-deploy. The Phase-7 deferral note claims post-snapshot dirs are "covered going-forward by the Phase-3 orphan sweep" — false for registered sessions. The fix is cheap (the boot-time reconcile+finalize sweep must target ALL terminal-status unmeasured sessions with a reachable live-root sidecar, not just the no-row orphans), but as drafted this is a silent multi-week hole spanning the entire build period, and the plan's own outcome accounting (69+37+3) would never notice it.

The forward orphan sweep mints "honest `measured-backfill` records going forward" — reusing the exact provenance label criterion 4 defines for the one-shot historical tool. Two different pipelines (a periodic live sweep with quiesce timing vs a one-shot offline run against a frozen snapshot) now share one provenance value, which is precisely what "auditable forever" forbids: an auditor can no longer tell which code path, which sidecar root, and which evidence window produced a record. Give the forward sweep its own state (`measured-late` or `measured-orphan-sweep`), counted identically but distinguishable. This is a one-word schema decision that is nearly free now and a migration later — the plan's own foresight brief ("record shape needs no migration later") argues against its own label reuse.

findings.criterion: 3 ("a later live finalize can still measure")
findings.message: Criterion 3's second clause is permissive in the draft but never actuated: `finalize-deferred` is "retryable NON-TERMINAL," yet no component is tasked with retrying it. The reconcile-dead path fires on a transition that already happened; the boot sweep's scope is unstated (see Finding 5); the only surfaced consequence of accumulation is a yellow healthcheck WARN. The observed failure mode this effort exists to fix was "spend quietly returns to zeros" — this design refines that to "spend quietly accumulates in deferred," an improvement in honesty but not in outcome, and it makes the criterion's "CAN still measure" true only in the sense that a human could notice the WARN and do something unspecified. Specify the retry owner and cadence (e.g., the periodic sweep re-attempts every deferred terminal session whose sidecar is reachable) and add a test that a deferred record actually BECOMES measured without manual intervention.

findings.criterion: 2-satisfying receipt in wave one and earns trust while the risky substrate soaks. At minimum, justify why the separate-line render can't land early; "surfaces render real substrate output, not placeholders" doesn't hold here — the general record IS real substrate output that already exists.
findings.message: The one already-measured record (2.76M tok / 445s in `general`) needs only the rollup-line and render changes to become visible — no CAS, no parser, no pricing engine strictly required for a tokens+time line. The plan makes the user wait through five build phases before any surface shows anything, on a substrate-soak rationale that genuinely applies to the CAS but not to a read-only rollup line over an existing record. A competitor ships the cheap,

`measured-partial` (truncated sidecar tail) counts as a measured session and its undercounted tokens flow into the same rollup totals with no per-total qualifier — the usage-state distribution surfaces the ratio, but the headline token/dollar figures silently blend clean and truncated measurements. Criterion 6's spirit is that displayed aggregates not overstate their own precision; a total that includes known-partial members should carry a marker (e.g., "≥" or an asterisk keyed to the partial count), the same honesty device Phase 2 already applies to reconcile-only durations ("≤ Nh"). Cheap to add now while the render helper is being built.

The claim "record content is idempotent (same session → same payload) so a double-fire converges" is false as specified elsewhere in the same plan: the end-time evidence ladder (Phase 2) and the quiesce check mean two finalizes evaluated at different moments can compute different durations and different token tails, so payloads are NOT deterministic per session. The guarantee is the exclusive-create — one winner, loser discarded — and that alone. This matters because a Foreman wave could faithfully implement the stated invariant as a test ("double-fire produces byte-identical payloads") which cannot hold, or worse, weaken the claim file to allow "idempotent" rewrites. Strike the idempotency justification; state plainly that the winner's payload is authoritative and the loser writes nothing.

"Assert each estimate stays within a declared error band" — against what? The sidecar carries no costUSD (the intake's own evidence), so the fixture test can only compare the pricing function's output to a hand-computed application of the same table: a tautology that pins arithmetic, not accuracy. That's fine and worth having, but the plan should say so honestly rather than implying the band validates estimate fidelity — otherwise the test's green reads as "estimates verified within N%" when nothing external was ever consulted. The real protections here are the "est." label and the `as_of` date; the band language overclaims in a plan whose brand is honesty.

findings.criterion: 3 (latch cannot be burned hermetically) + 4 (never overwrites a live-measured record)
findings.message: Phase 2 promises to "reclassify the 3 poisoned `sidecar-root-unavailable` records to `finalize-deferred` so the Phase 6 backfill may still measure them." Phase 7 then brags that "an existing live-measured cost file wins BY CONSTRUCTION — no compare-and-decide code path exists to get wrong." These cannot both be true. If the hermetic finalize consumed the CAS, a claim/cost file exists for those 3 sessions; the exclusive-create semantics the plan celebrates will refuse the backfill mint for exactly the sessions the repair path promises to rescue. Repairing them requires either deleting the burned claim file or adding a compare-and-decide path — the very code path Phase 7 declares nonexistent. The plan must say which: a one-shot audited claim-file deletion in the repair step (with its own test), or an admission that the 3 stay unmeasured. Right now it sells both sides of the contradiction as design virtues.

findings.criterion: 3 (a finalize in a hermetic context skips without consuming the CAS)
findings.message: The plan inverts the predicate to "only a finalize presenting the matching boot beacon may consume the CAS," but never states who is allowed to WRITE a beacon. The daily healthcheck boots the same `anchor_gui.py` server code on port 8778; if server startup writes the beacon, the hermetic healthcheck context mints itself a valid identity and the observed poison vector walks straight through the new gate. So beacon-writing needs its own hermetic predicate — which is circular: the blocklist problem the inversion claims to eliminate reappears one layer down, unexamined. Additionally, positive identity over-rotates in the other direction: a manually-run debug server (documented as legitimate in CLAUDE.md when the service is stopped) and any non-NSSM deployment (the shareable distro the foresight brief explicitly claims to serve) present no NSSM beacon and therefore defer FOREVER — capture silently stops in legitimate live contexts. The plan needs to define beacon-mint authority and the non-NSSM live path explicitly, or criterion 3 is fixed on paper and broken in both directions in practice.

findings.criterion: 3 (regression-tested hermetic-skip) and 1 (swarm spend visible going forward)
findings.message: The plan merges and deploys ONCE, at Phase 8. The intake evidence says the hermetic-burn vector is live today and the healthcheck fires daily at 5 AM; every day of a 7-phase FULL-depth build is another day sessions can be permanently poisoned and every fleet run during the build window is spend lost or degraded to sweep-recovery. This effort's own memory record (telemetry-resume) names merged-not-deployed as a recurring failure mode — and this plan institutionalizes it for the highest-risk fix. The CAS+beacon substrate (Phase 2) is self-contained and independently deployable; an investor asks why the bleeding isn't stopped in week one. The plan should name an interim deploy checkpoint after the substrate phase, or justify explicitly why one deploy is safer.

The plan specifies the table shape (per-model per-category rates, as_of date, unknown-model refusal) but never defines what the number MEANS. "Subscription-equivalent" is ambiguous between at least two wildly different quantities: (a) what these tokens WOULD cost at API list price, and (b) an amortized share of the flat Max subscription fee. These can differ by an order of magnitude, and the whole effort's banner is HONEST telemetry. A number rendered "$X.XX est." whose definition the maintainer can't state is not honestly provenanced — it's a decorated guess. The plan must pin the formula (recommend: API-list-price equivalent, labeled as such) and state it in the render label, not just the plan text. Fixture tests asserting "within a declared error band" are meaningless until the band is relative to a defined quantity.

The intake evidence hands the plan a free receipt: one already-measured record (2.76M tok / 445s) sitting in `general`, invisible only because of `ROLLUP_LANES`. Rendering the separate general/interactive line is a small additive rollup change plus display — no CAS, no parser fence, no pricing engine required (tokens and seconds render without the dollar column). The plan defers this to Phase 6, behind four substrate phases, so John sees zero new numbers for most of the effort. The stated justification ("surfaces render real substrate output, not placeholders") doesn't apply to this record — it IS real substrate output, already on disk. Pull the tokens/time portion of criterion 2 forward as the first visible receipt; leave only the est.-$ column gated on Phase 5.

findings.criterion: 1 (a new fleet run produces measured records) + Stage-0 decision 2
findings.section: Phase 4 — orphan-sidecar sweep / deferred orchestrator wiring
findings.message: Decision 2 defines `measured-backfill` as the provenance of HISTORICAL recovery — "auditable forever" depends on the label meaning one thing. Phase 4's forward orphan sweep mints `measured-backfill` for any future unregistered launch, and Phase 4 simultaneously defers the enumeration of which orchestrators get wired through the choke-point helper to Stage 2. Net effect: an unknown fraction of FUTURE fleet runs will land with backfill provenance indefinitely, which (a) destroys the audit meaning of the label — you can no longer distinguish "recovered history" from "launch path we never finished wiring," and (b) lets criterion 1's live proof (Phase 8's fleet run) pass technically while the eager-finalize path it's supposed to prove goes unexercised. Mint forward sweep recoveries under a distinct state (e.g. `measured-sweep`), and require the Phase 8 receipt to show `measured` — not any measured-* — for the fleet run's sub-agents.

The phase both "verifies count ≥ the 55 observed at intake" and "logs any present-then vs present-now delta honestly." If pruning already struck between 2026-07-18 and execution, these conflict: does a count of 51 fail the phase or merely get logged? Unstated. Also, the window between this snapshot and the Phase-3 sweep going live is explicitly uncovered ("no second backfill mode is built") — sidecars created during the multi-phase build can be pruned before the sweep deploys, and the plan should say honestly that those are accepted losses rather than leaving the gap implicit.

"Confirm the coverage-report ratio moved" is not a success test — any nonzero backfill moves the ratio. The intake gives exact numbers (69 no-usage-state + 37 uncorrelated + 3 repaired; 55+ sidecar dirs), so the plan can and should pre-commit an expected recovery envelope (e.g. "≥ 50 of the 109 target sessions recovered or explicitly dispositioned as no-sidecar/ambiguous") and treat a large shortfall as a finding, not a shrug. As written, the final receipt for criterion 4 cannot fail, which means it verifies nothing.

findings.section: Overview ("All 29 integrated ideas and all 16 premortem mitigations are placed")
findings.message: The plan advertises that every single ideation output survived into a phase. A Master Plan that cuts nothing has done no prioritization, and there is no wave-count, token-budget, or duration estimate anywhere — the investor is asked to fund FULL depth on an unbounded bill. At minimum, name the ideas that are load-bearing for a criterion vs. conventions-completeness (CLI mirror, coverage report, second healthcheck WARN) so Stage 2 can shed the latter under budget pressure without re-litigating the plan.

If, under the new scheme, that consumption maps to an existing claim/cost file, then by (a) and (b) the backfill's exclusive-create will lose to the poisoned artifact and the sessions stay unmeasured — the repair is dead on arrival. If instead the repair deletes or supersedes the poisoned artifact, then a "rewrite a consumed latch" code path exists, and (a)/(b) are false as universal claims — and that path needs its own guard so only THIS class of record is ever repairable, or the never-overwrite guarantee for live-measured records rests on convention rather than construction. The draft never says which; the ambiguity sits precisely on the highest-risk primitive the risk taxonomy names.

findings.topic: beacon issuance is unscoped — hermetic servers can mint beacons
findings.message: The inversion from blocklist to positive identity only works if beacon ISSUANCE is itself positively scoped, and the draft never specifies that. The healthcheck boots a real throwaway server on 8778 running the same anchor_gui boot path; preview servers boot the same code on OS-assigned ports. If "the live NSSM service writes a boot beacon at startup" is implemented as "server boot writes a beacon," every hermetic server is a beacon-holder and the poison vector recurs wearing a badge. If issuance is instead gated on "not healthcheck, not redirected data dir, not test port," the design has smuggled the blocklist back in — the exact enumerate-the-hermetic-contexts fragility idea 5 claims to eliminate. The predicate needs a stated positive anchor (e.g., beacon written iff the process holds the exclusive 8777 bind on the real data dir, verified at write time), and the STUB-GATE trio needs a fourth case: a fully-booted NON-8777 server attempting finalize with its own self-issued beacon must defer. Without that case, the regression tests validate the mechanism against the previous failure's shape, not the next one's.

findings.topic: snapshot verification baseline does not exist
findings.message: The phase promises to "verify count ≥ the 55 observed at intake" and to "log any dirs present-then vs present-now delta honestly in the manifest." This is unfalsifiable as written: the intake evidence recorded a COUNT ("55+ sidecar dirs"), not an enumeration of dirnames. Without a then-list, a per-dir delta cannot be computed, and "count ≥ 55" cannot detect a prune-and-grow substitution (e.g., 10 historical dirs pruned since 2026-07-18 while 12 new ones appeared — the check passes while history criterion 4 depends on is already gone). The honest version of this task is: snapshot NOW, enumerate what was captured, and state plainly that losses between intake and snapshot are UNDETECTABLE — reconciling instead against the registry's known session-id set (which sessions have a matching archived dir vs not) to bound what the backfill can possibly recover. As drafted, the manifest performs an audit it lacks the evidence to perform, which is exactly the kind of confidence-without-provenance this North Star exists to eliminate.

findings.topic: backfill run window never scheduled
findings.message: The backfill tool "REFUSES to run while the service is reachable unless --force," but the phase ordering puts the backfill run (Phase 6) BEFORE merge+deploy (Phase 7), while the production service is live on 8777 throughout the build. The plan therefore never says when the required service outage happens: either a build wave takes production down mid-effort (unstated, and it should be a deliberate, drained stop per the warm-restart convention), or the backfill actually runs inside Phase 7's deploy window (making the phase ordering wrong as written), or — the failure mode the discipline exists to prevent — the builder reaches for `--force` because the refusal fires on the first real run. A run-discipline feature whose happy path is unreachable in the plan's own sequence trains the operator to use the escape hatch. Name the outage: when, how (drain), and which phase owns it.

findings.topic: orphan-sweep records have no attribution target
findings.message: The sweep mints `measured-backfill` records for sidecars "whose dirname embeds a valid session marker but has no registry row," claiming "an unregistered launch degrades to late-measured, never invisible." But the Phase-2 frozen record schema requires `lane`, `effort_id`/`chain_id`, and the rollup surfaces are per-project per-lane — a session with no registry row has none of these. Where does this record actually SURFACE? If nowhere, "never invisible" is an assertion about a file on disk, not about spend a user can see, and the criterion is met in letter only. Specify the attribution fallback (e.g., an "unattributed" line on the rollup) or honestly rename the guarantee. Relatedly, the `id-unverified` path (idea 1) never states whether such a session's spend is measured under the observed id or excluded — same ambiguity, same fix needed.

findings.topic: finalize-deferred write target unspecified
findings.message: File EXISTENCE under `.anchor/run-costs/` IS the CAS. The plan says a non-beacon context "records retryable NON-TERMINAL usage_state: finalize-deferred" — but never says WHERE. If the deferral stamp is written anywhere on the claim path, the act of deferring consumes the latch, recreating the original bug with a politer label. The plan must pin the invariant explicitly — deferred/skipped/unrecognized states live ONLY on the registry record; the claim file is created by nothing except a successful measured write — and the STUB-GATE hermetic-skip test must assert the claim file's NON-existence after the skip, not merely that a later finalize succeeds.

findings.topic: synthetic-predicate loud-fail test is self-contradictory
findings.message: The predicate is defined as "an explicit synthetic=True registration flag … never name-sniffing," yet the convention test promises that "registering synthetic without the flag fails loudly." Detecting an UNflagged synthetic registration requires recognizing syntheticness by some signal other than the flag — i.e., name-sniffing, the thing just forbidden. As written the test is unimplementable; what's actually implementable is (a) the known synthetic REGISTRARS (doctor, healthcheck) are asserted to pass the flag, and (b) all surfaces route through the predicate. Say that instead. Separately, "__doctor__ migrates onto the flag" is stated as code behavior but the registry already CONTAINS historical `__doctor__` rows without the flag — the exclusion of criterion 2 needs a data migration (or a one-time legacy shim, honestly labeled), not just new registration code.

findings.topic: pricing error-band test is circular
findings.message: "Fixture-test a cache-read-dominated session and a mixed-model session; assert each estimate stays within a declared error band" — within a band relative to WHAT ground truth? There is no external reference for a subscription-equivalent estimate; the test necessarily computes the expected value from the same table and formula it is testing, proving arithmetic determinism, not estimate validity. A skeptical reader should not be shown "error band" language that implies calibration that doesn't exist. Either declare the honest test (golden-value regression pinning the formula against hand-computed fixtures, so a table or formula change turns a test red) or, if a real band is intended, name its reference point. The "est." label carries the honesty load here — don't let the test suite overclaim what the label correctly underclaims.

findings.topic: real-sidecar fixture PII exposure
findings.message: "Pin a CAPTURED REAL sidecar as a test fixture" commits a real engine transcript — conversation content, file paths, potentially secrets from whatever that historical session touched — into the repo. The project runs a no-PII/secrets scan in `distro.py` and this repo already leaks-by-default per the 2026-07-17 review; a raw sidecar fixture is a new instance of the same class. The fixture's VALUE is its field shape and envelope names, not its content — the plan should require a shape-preserving sanitization step (real structure, scrubbed strings, token counts kept) and state that the fixture passes the distro scan. Cheap to fix now, expensive after it's committed.

findings.topic: double phase numbering
findings.message: Every heading carries two conflicting ordinals ("Phase 1 — Phase 0 — …" through "Phase 8 — Phase 7 — …"), and the success-criteria block appears twice (verbatim North Star + a paraphrased summary). Stage 2 wave mapping, Foreman handoff, and Shark convergence all key on phase identity; an off-by-one label scheme invites cross-references to the wrong phase. Pick one numbering and delete the duplicate criteria block.

reviews.note: Reviewed as Contrarian Shark through the competitor lens — pressing where a rival plan would beat this one on correctness of the capture predicate, irreversible-loss handling, real swarm coverage, and time-to-first-receipt. All findings judged strictly against the locked North Star.

findings.topic: beacon predicate vs legitimate non-service writers
findings.criterion: 3 (latch cannot be burned hermetically) and 4 (history recovered)
findings.message: The plan contradicts itself on who may consume the CAS. Phase 2 locks consumption to "only a finalize presenting the matching beacon" — a boot beacon written by the live NSSM service — and routes every non-beacon context to `finalize-deferred`. Phase 7's backfill tool then, BY DESIGN, runs while the service is DOWN (it probes 8777 and refuses to run if reachable) and "uses the IDENTICAL exclusive-create claim files as the live path." A stopped service means no valid beacon (dead PID, stale token), so under the Phase-2 predicate as written the backfill is structurally a non-beacon context and cannot mint a single record — criterion 4 is unimplementable against criterion 3's own mechanism. The same hole swallows every other legitimate out-of-process writer: the warm-drain script (`pre_restart_drain.py`, a separate elevated process), any future CLI-side finalize, the forced backfill mode. The plan needs an explicit authorization story (e.g., beacon-OR-service-verifiably-down, or a distinct backfill credential) specified now, not discovered at Foreman time. A competitor plan would define the trust model for ALL writers, not just the happy-path service process.

findings.topic: snapshot-time filtering risks irreversible loss
findings.message: Phase 0 copies "every sidecar dir whose dirname embeds an `…anchor-worktrees-<session_id>` munged cwd" — i.e., it FILTERS at snapshot time using a munging matcher that isn't isolated and regression-tested until Phase 2/3. This inverts the whole rationale for snapshotting NOW. If the preliminary matcher misses a dirname variant (different munging across engine versions, path-length truncation, casing), the excluded dirs are then pruned by engine retention and are gone forever — the exact irreversible loss the snapshot exists to prevent — and no later phase can detect the omission because the evidence no longer exists. The snapshot must be OVER-inclusive (copy the entire sidecar root, or at minimum everything matching a maximally loose pattern) and defer all filtering to Phase 6 where the hardened matcher lives. Bytes are cheap; a false-negative at snapshot time is permanent. The "verify count ≥ 55" check does not save this: it validates the matcher against itself.

findings.topic: choke-point helper misses skill-layer swarm launches
findings.message: The choke-point launch helper plus a "conformance test [that] greps PRODUCT CODE for raw spawn calls" structurally cannot cover the dominant swarm source: skill-layer dispatch (the 5:1 agy/orchestrator pattern), where sub-agent CLI processes are spawned by the model INSIDE a session, not by Anchor product code. That is precisely how the 106 observed swarm sessions came to exist unmeasured. The plan's own deferral ("orchestrators not yet routed through the helper… enumeration in Stage 2") quietly punts the enumeration that decides whether criterion 1 is met at all — and the Phase-8 live proof ("trigger one small real fleet run and confirm measured records") has no stated fallback if that run's launcher turns out to be unwired. A competitor plan would name the concrete launch surfaces (which orchestrators, which dispatcher scripts) in the MASTER plan and state which are in-scope, because "where wired" with an empty wired set trivially satisfies the letter of the criterion while producing zero new measured swarm records. Demand the enumeration be a Stage-1 commitment, not a Stage-2 discovery.

findings.topic: legacy __doctor__ records have no flag-migration path
findings.message: The synthetic predicate is "driven by an explicit `synthetic=True` registration flag (marker convention, NEVER name-sniffing)." But every `__doctor__` session already in the registry was registered before the flag existed and carries no marker — under a strict never-name-sniff rule those legacy records classify as non-synthetic and LEAK into every spend surface, directly violating "excluded everywhere." The plan needs a named one-shot migration stamping the flag onto existing doctor records (which unavoidably identifies them by name — acceptable as a one-time migration, but it must be admitted and specified, not left to collide with the stated rule). Relatedly, the loud-failure test ("registering synthetic without the flag fails loudly") is circular as written: detecting an unflagged synthetic registration requires exactly the name-sniffing the convention forbids. Specify what actually enforces it.

findings.topic: coverage hole between snapshot and substrate deploy
findings.criterion: 1 and 4 (every class of run session measured or honestly reported)
findings.message: Sessions that finish AFTER the Phase-0 snapshot but BEFORE the Phase-3 substrate deploys fall through every net in the plan: they are not in the frozen snapshot (backfill reads the snapshot "exclusively"), live finalize didn't exist when they ended, the orphan sweep explicitly targets only sidecars "with no registry row" (these sessions HAVE rows), and reconcile-dead finalize fires on the transition, which already happened pre-deploy. The Phase-7 deferral note claims post-snapshot dirs are "covered going-forward by the Phase-3 orphan sweep" — false for registered sessions. The fix is cheap (the boot-time reconcile+finalize sweep must target ALL terminal-status unmeasured sessions with a reachable live-root sidecar, not just the no-row orphans), but as drafted this is a silent multi-week hole spanning the entire build period, and the plan's own outcome accounting (69+37+3) would never notice it.

findings.topic: measured-backfill label collision between two pipelines
findings.message: The forward orphan sweep mints "honest `measured-backfill` records going forward" — reusing the exact provenance label criterion 4 defines for the one-shot historical tool. Two different pipelines (a periodic live sweep with quiesce timing vs a one-shot offline run against a frozen snapshot) now share one provenance value, which is precisely what "auditable forever" forbids: an auditor can no longer tell which code path, which sidecar root, and which evidence window produced a record. Give the forward sweep its own state (`measured-late` or `measured-orphan-sweep`), counted identically but distinguishable. This is a one-word schema decision that is nearly free now and a migration later — the plan's own foresight brief ("record shape needs no migration later") argues against its own label reuse.

findings.topic: finalize-deferred has no retry mechanism
findings.criterion: 3 ("a later live finalize can still measure")
findings.message: Criterion 3's second clause is permissive in the draft but never actuated: `finalize-deferred` is "retryable NON-TERMINAL," yet no component is tasked with retrying it. The reconcile-dead path fires on a transition that already happened; the boot sweep's scope is unstated (see Finding 5); the only surfaced consequence of accumulation is a yellow healthcheck WARN. The observed failure mode this effort exists to fix was "spend quietly returns to zeros" — this design refines that to "spend quietly accumulates in deferred," an improvement in honesty but not in outcome, and it makes the criterion's "CAN still measure" true only in the sense that a human could notice the WARN and do something unspecified. Specify the retry owner and cadence (e.g., the periodic sweep re-attempts every deferred terminal session whose sidecar is reachable) and add a test that a deferred record actually BECOMES measured without manual intervention.

findings.topic: first visible receipt deferred to Phase 5 of 7
findings.criterion: 2-satisfying receipt in wave one and earns trust while the risky substrate soaks. At minimum, justify why the separate-line render can't land early; "surfaces render real substrate output, not placeholders" doesn't hold here — the general record IS real substrate output that already exists.
findings.message: The one already-measured record (2.76M tok / 445s in `general`) needs only the rollup-line and render changes to become visible — no CAS, no parser, no pricing engine strictly required for a tokens+time line. The plan makes the user wait through five build phases before any surface shows anything, on a substrate-soak rationale that genuinely applies to the CAS but not to a read-only rollup line over an existing record. A competitor ships the cheap,

findings.topic: measured-partial counted identically to measured
findings.message: `measured-partial` (truncated sidecar tail) counts as a measured session and its undercounted tokens flow into the same rollup totals with no per-total qualifier — the usage-state distribution surfaces the ratio, but the headline token/dollar figures silently blend clean and truncated measurements. Criterion 6's spirit is that displayed aggregates not overstate their own precision; a total that includes known-partial members should carry a marker (e.g., "≥" or an asterisk keyed to the partial count), the same honesty device Phase 2 already applies to reconcile-only durations ("≤ Nh"). Cheap to add now while the render helper is being built.

findings.topic: false idempotent-payload justification for the CAS
findings.message: The claim "record content is idempotent (same session → same payload) so a double-fire converges" is false as specified elsewhere in the same plan: the end-time evidence ladder (Phase 2) and the quiesce check mean two finalizes evaluated at different moments can compute different durations and different token tails, so payloads are NOT deterministic per session. The guarantee is the exclusive-create — one winner, loser discarded — and that alone. This matters because a Foreman wave could faithfully implement the stated invariant as a test ("double-fire produces byte-identical payloads") which cannot hold, or worse, weaken the claim file to allow "idempotent" rewrites. Strike the idempotency justification; state plainly that the winner's payload is authoritative and the loser writes nothing.

findings.topic: estimate error-band test has no ground truth
findings.message: "Assert each estimate stays within a declared error band" — against what? The sidecar carries no costUSD (the intake's own evidence), so the fixture test can only compare the pricing function's output to a hand-computed application of the same table: a tautology that pins arithmetic, not accuracy. That's fine and worth having, but the plan should say so honestly rather than implying the band validates estimate fidelity — otherwise the test's green reads as "estimates verified within N%" when nothing external was ever consulted. The real protections here are the "est." label and the `as_of` date; the band language overclaims in a plan whose brand is honesty.

findings.topic: double phase numbering
findings.criterion: (plan mechanics serving all criteria via the Foreman handoff)
findings.message: Every header reads "## Phase N — Phase N-1 — title" (e.g., "Phase 1 — Phase 0", "Phase 7 — Phase 6"). Two live numbering schemes in a document destined for mechanical wave-parsing (Foreman, locate-plan) is an invitation for a wave-mapping error — cross-references inside the draft already use the inner scheme ("Phase 6 backfill", "Phase-3 orphan sweep") while the headers sort by the outer one. Collapse to one scheme before Stage 2.

reviews.note: Reviewed through the bored-investor lens: where does the money show up, when, and is any number in this plan falsifiable. The plan is thorough on mechanism and weak on payoff timing, deploy cadence, and the meaning of its own headline dollar figure. Two internal contradictions in the safety substrate are BLOCKER-grade.

findings.topic: poisoned-CAS repair contradicts no-overwrite-by-construction
findings.criterion: 3 (latch cannot be burned hermetically) + 4 (never overwrites a live-measured record)
findings.message: Phase 2 promises to "reclassify the 3 poisoned `sidecar-root-unavailable` records to `finalize-deferred` so the Phase 6 backfill may still measure them." Phase 7 then brags that "an existing live-measured cost file wins BY CONSTRUCTION — no compare-and-decide code path exists to get wrong." These cannot both be true. If the hermetic finalize consumed the CAS, a claim/cost file exists for those 3 sessions; the exclusive-create semantics the plan celebrates will refuse the backfill mint for exactly the sessions the repair path promises to rescue. Repairing them requires either deleting the burned claim file or adding a compare-and-decide path — the very code path Phase 7 declares nonexistent. The plan must say which: a one-shot audited claim-file deletion in the repair step (with its own test), or an admission that the 3 stay unmeasured. Right now it sells both sides of the contradiction as design virtues.

findings.topic: beacon minting has no hermetic discriminator
findings.criterion: 3 (a finalize in a hermetic context skips without consuming the CAS)
findings.message: The plan inverts the predicate to "only a finalize presenting the matching boot beacon may consume the CAS," but never states who is allowed to WRITE a beacon. The daily healthcheck boots the same `anchor_gui.py` server code on port 8778; if server startup writes the beacon, the hermetic healthcheck context mints itself a valid identity and the observed poison vector walks straight through the new gate. So beacon-writing needs its own hermetic predicate — which is circular: the blocklist problem the inversion claims to eliminate reappears one layer down, unexamined. Additionally, positive identity over-rotates in the other direction: a manually-run debug server (documented as legitimate in CLAUDE.md when the service is stopped) and any non-NSSM deployment (the shareable distro the foresight brief explicitly claims to serve) present no NSSM beacon and therefore defer FOREVER — capture silently stops in legitimate live contexts. The plan needs to define beacon-mint authority and the non-NSSM live path explicitly, or criterion 3 is fixed on paper and broken in both directions in practice.

findings.topic: single big-bang deploy while the poison vector stays live
findings.criterion: 3 (regression-tested hermetic-skip) and 1 (swarm spend visible going forward)
findings.message: The plan merges and deploys ONCE, at Phase 8. The intake evidence says the hermetic-burn vector is live today and the healthcheck fires daily at 5 AM; every day of a 7-phase FULL-depth build is another day sessions can be permanently poisoned and every fleet run during the build window is spend lost or degraded to sweep-recovery. This effort's own memory record (telemetry-resume) names merged-not-deployed as a recurring failure mode — and this plan institutionalizes it for the highest-risk fix. The CAS+beacon substrate (Phase 2) is self-contained and independently deployable; an investor asks why the bleeding isn't stopped in week one. The plan should name an interim deploy checkpoint after the substrate phase, or justify explicitly why one deploy is safer.

findings.topic: "subscription-equivalent" dollar semantics undefined
findings.message: The plan specifies the table shape (per-model per-category rates, as_of date, unknown-model refusal) but never defines what the number MEANS. "Subscription-equivalent" is ambiguous between at least two wildly different quantities: (a) what these tokens WOULD cost at API list price, and (b) an amortized share of the flat Max subscription fee. These can differ by an order of magnitude, and the whole effort's banner is HONEST telemetry. A number rendered "$X.XX est." whose definition the maintainer can't state is not honestly provenanced — it's a decorated guess. The plan must pin the formula (recommend: API-list-price equivalent, labeled as such) and state it in the render label, not just the plan text. Fixture tests asserting "within a declared error band" are meaningless until the band is relative to a defined quantity.

findings.topic: cheapest visible win deferred behind five phases
findings.message: The intake evidence hands the plan a free receipt: one already-measured record (2.76M tok / 445s) sitting in `general`, invisible only because of `ROLLUP_LANES`. Rendering the separate general/interactive line is a small additive rollup change plus display — no CAS, no parser fence, no pricing engine required (tokens and seconds render without the dollar column). The plan defers this to Phase 6, behind four substrate phases, so John sees zero new numbers for most of the effort. The stated justification ("surfaces render real substrate output, not placeholders") doesn't apply to this record — it IS real substrate output, already on disk. Pull the tokens/time portion of criterion 2 forward as the first visible receipt; leave only the est.-$ column gated on Phase 5.

findings.topic: forward capture conflates measured-backfill provenance
findings.section: Phase 4 — orphan-sidecar sweep / deferred orchestrator wiring
findings.criterion: 1 (a new fleet run produces measured records) + Stage-0 decision 2
findings.message: Decision 2 defines `measured-backfill` as the provenance of HISTORICAL recovery — "auditable forever" depends on the label meaning one thing. Phase 4's forward orphan sweep mints `measured-backfill` for any future unregistered launch, and Phase 4 simultaneously defers the enumeration of which orchestrators get wired through the choke-point helper to Stage 2. Net effect: an unknown fraction of FUTURE fleet runs will land with backfill provenance indefinitely, which (a) destroys the audit meaning of the label — you can no longer distinguish "recovered history" from "launch path we never finished wiring," and (b) lets criterion 1's live proof (Phase 8's fleet run) pass technically while the eager-finalize path it's supposed to prove goes unexercised. Mint forward sweep recoveries under a distinct state (e.g. `measured-sweep`), and require the Phase 8 receipt to show `measured` — not any measured-* — for the fleet run's sub-agents.

findings.topic: snapshot failure semantics contradictory
findings.message: The phase both "verifies count ≥ the 55 observed at intake" and "logs any present-then vs present-now delta honestly." If pruning already struck between 2026-07-18 and execution, these conflict: does a count of 51 fail the phase or merely get logged? Unstated. Also, the window between this snapshot and the Phase-3 sweep going live is explicitly uncovered ("no second backfill mode is built") — sidecars created during the multi-phase build can be pruned before the sweep deploys, and the plan should say honestly that those are accepted losses rather than leaving the gap implicit.

findings.topic: unfalsifiable ship receipt
findings.message: "Confirm the coverage-report ratio moved" is not a success test — any nonzero backfill moves the ratio. The intake gives exact numbers (69 no-usage-state + 37 uncorrelated + 3 repaired; 55+ sidecar dirs), so the plan can and should pre-commit an expected recovery envelope (e.g. "≥ 50 of the 109 target sessions recovered or explicitly dispositioned as no-sidecar/ambiguous") and treat a large shortfall as a finding, not a shrug. As written, the final receipt for criterion 4 cannot fail, which means it verifies nothing.

findings.topic: no cost/wave budget, zero ideas cut
findings.section: Overview ("All 29 integrated ideas and all 16 premortem mitigations are placed")
findings.message: The plan advertises that every single ideation output survived into a phase. A Master Plan that cuts nothing has done no prioritization, and there is no wave-count, token-budget, or duration estimate anywhere — the investor is asked to fund FULL depth on an unbounded bill. At minimum, name the ideas that are load-bearing for a criterion vs. conventions-completeness (CLI mirror, coverage report, second healthcheck WARN) so Stage 2 can shed the latter under budget pressure without re-litigating the plan.

findings.topic: double phase numbering
findings.message: "Phase 1 — Phase 0", "Phase 2 — Phase 1" etc. is an off-by-one collision that will propagate into Stage 2 wave references and Foreman handoff labels ("Phase 6" means two different phases depending on which numbering you read). Pick one scheme before Stage 2. The draft also pastes the full North Star and then repeats the success criteria immediately after — redundant bulk in a document Sharks and the Judge must re-read every round.
